A1.justification: Despite changed titles and framing, both PDFs describe the same underlying VQA research, with matching architectures, dataset composition and experiments. All 25 pages of v3 and 19 pages of v4, including appendices, figures, tables and equations, support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original teacher–student experiments, component comparisons and iterative-training results across ten benchmarks in Table 1, Figure 4 and Appendix Table 5.

after.justification: v4 reports original ranking-model results, supervised fine-tuning, ablations and pairwise prediction accuracies in Tables 2–4 and 6.

M1.justification: v4 retains the multimodal backbone, motion branch and soft-ranking inference, but removes v3's auxiliary confidence-loss objective and explicit gMAD/misclassification-based difficult-sample selection from the proposed procedure. It presents standard pairwise SFT with iterative label refinement and adds a two-label hard-ranking variant alongside five-label soft ranking.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same ten evaluation benchmarks, social-media source pool, content categories and synthetic distortion families. The 438k-video/700k-pair composition already appears in v3 Table 2 and is retained as PLVD in v4 Table 1. Added fine-tuning and accuracy evaluations use existing coverage.

E2.justification: v4's main comparison removes VQA2 and VQAThinker and adds NIQE, IL-NIQE, VIIDEO, STEM, TPQI and BUONA-VISTA, with the latter two reporting only some in-domain results. New supervised comparisons include TLVQM, VIDEVAL, VSFA, PatchVQ and SimpleVQA; Table 6 adds general-purpose LMM and teacher-ensemble comparators.

E3.justification: The pairwise-training appendices change the learning rate from 1e-4 to 1e-5 and per-device batch size from two to one. The stated histogram-matching target changes from LSVQ to four aggregated UGC benchmarks. v4 adds supervised fine-tuning with ten-fold cross-validation, pairwise-accuracy evaluation and a data-matched label-refinement control. These are reported protocol changes; they do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds hard-versus-soft ranking, motion-encoder ablation, pretraining-versus-no-pretraining comparisons, and a control testing label refinement while holding the training set fixed. It removes v3's individual-teacher transfer study and confidence-loss ablation. Synthetic-distortion and iterative-stage analyses remain, with revised comparisons.

E5.justification: v4 Table 3 newly specifies ten-fold cross-validation for KoNViD-1k, LIVE-VQC and YouTube-UGC, adding resampling information for the supervised evaluation. Neither version reports seed counts, confidence intervals or performance variability; no increase in repetitions of existing experiments is established.

E6.justification: v3 Table 1 model V reports overall OOD SRCC/PLCC of 0.745/0.789; v4 Table 2 Stage 3 reports 0.716/0.752 under revised training, so this is not a same-setting performance comparison. v3 model II's results are retained as v4 Soft Ranking Stage 1. Hard-ranking, supervised-transfer, ablation and pairwise-accuracy entries are added, while individual-teacher student results are removed.

T1.justification: v3's formal gMAD selection objective and adaptive confidence-loss equations are removed, while v4 introduces binary-ranking token and aggregation-weight definitions. The central soft-ranking/Thurstone-MAP formulation and distortion formulas remain, with architecture equations moved into the main text. Neither version develops a theorem-and-proof framework.

C1.justification: v3 centers its contribution on establishing a distinct weak-to-strong generalization effect and improving it through diverse teachers and difficult examples. v4 centers ranking-based self-supervision, emphasizes the existing PLVD dataset as a contribution, and adds a claim of state-of-the-art performance after supervised fine-tuning. The broad generalization objective remains.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations concerning soft ranking's quality-distance information, temporal-encoder limitations on LIVE-VQC, and refinement benefits beyond additional training data. It removes explanations centered on confidence loss and difficult-sample W2S learning. A new explicit limitation identifies the inference cost of comparing each video against five anchors.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies anchor selection using five quality intervals and minimum inter-model variance, plus inference on two RTX 3090 GPUs. It revises training configuration disclosures and changes the advertised repository from W2S-VQA to a promised LMM-PVQA code/data release. The parameter-count table and permissive-license filtering statement disappear; most preprocessing and distortion recipes remain.

R1.justification: The dedicated weak-to-strong literature discussion and its principal citations disappear, replaced by expanded opinion-unaware VQA and dataset positioning. v4 adds LLM-as-judge motivation and references for new comparators. v3's explicit architectural attribution to LMM-VQA is also removed, although the corresponding architecture is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten. A dataset–method–experiments structure replaces the separate W2S demonstration and improvement sections, and architecture details move from the appendix into the main text. The title, author block and terminology also change.

P2.justification: v4 switches to a two-column layout, creates a composite overview figure and redraws the model diagram for pairwise hard/soft ranking. Dataset statistics and the distribution plot move into the main text; comparison tables gain new groups and columns, and supervised/ablation/accuracy tables are added. The individual-teacher performance figure and parameter table are removed.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens diagnostic evaluation through the data-matched refinement control, supervised-transfer tests and explicit inference-cost limitation. However, it removes VQA2/VQAThinker comparisons and individual-teacher evidence, while its new pairwise-accuracy evaluation lacks a documented pair-sampling protocol. These gains and losses leave the net direction of overall paper quality uncertain; the changed performance numbers alone do not resolve it.
